title: Saving a part with its number unchanged is never refused as a duplicate
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete' and See Financial Data.
  • You can switch to a second location, {Location-B} (for example Staging Lethbridge - 4310), in the location switcher in the top bar.
  • Two active parts, {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-UNCH-01) and {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTESTPLUNCH01), are stocked at {Location-A} on two different Part Library entries, and their numbers match once upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces are ignored.
custom_steps:
1. At {Location-A}, go to Parts → Inventory and type {Part-B} in the search.
  2. Click the {Part-B} row.
  3. Change the Sell Price to 25.00.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Type {Part-A} in the search.
  6. Click the {Part-A} row.
  7. Change the Sell Price to 26.00.
  8. Click Save.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: the save goes through with no "already exists at this location" message. The window closes and the {Part-B} row shows Sell Price $25.00.
  • Step 8: the save goes through with no "already exists at this location" message. The window closes and the {Part-A} row shows Sell Price $26.00. Both parts keep their own numbers, {Part-A} and {Part-B}.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S7-N5b, §4 Key Decisions, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas board 2.1 (The part as it stands), 13 Oct copy. Tech plan §6 Phase 6 (ChangePartCommandHandler). Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S7-N5b: “S7-N3 and S7-N4 apply when a part is created and when its part number is changed. Saving a part with its number unchanged is never refused by them, even when the location already holds a part whose number matches it.”
  • PRD §4 Key Decisions (duplicate at the location): “A new part number already stocked at the location is refused, ignoring case and punctuation. This check stops a second copy of a part at one location. It runs when a part is created or its number is changed, never when a part is saved with its number unchanged.”
  • Tech plan, 7 Oct 2026, §6 Phase 6 backend (ChangePartCommandHandler): “the duplicate-at-location check (S7-N3/N4) runs only when the number changes, never on a save with the number unchanged (S7-N5b), so existing same-location duplicates keep saving”
